title: The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities
question: What is an option worth if you can hedge it continuously with the stock?
changed: A riskless hedge removes the expected return from the problem: the option's value solves a PDE whose solution is the Black–Scholes formula.
assumed: Constant volatility and rate, continuous frictionless trading, log-normal prices.

title: Theory of Rational Option Pricing
venue: The Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science
question: Which option properties follow from no-arbitrage alone, and how far does the hedging argument extend?
changed: Derived model-free bounds, extended Black–Scholes to dividends and stochastic rates, and put the replication argument on continuous-time footing.
assumed: A continuous dividend yield and frictionless markets.

title: The pricing of commodity contracts
question: How do you price options on futures and forwards?
changed: Black-76: write the option on the forward price and discount, so carry and dividends drop out of the formula.

title: The valuation of options for alternative stochastic processes
question: Is there a shortcut to option prices that avoids solving the hedging PDE?
changed: Risk-neutral valuation: since preferences drop out, price as if investors were risk neutral and discount at the riskless rate.

title: Option pricing when underlying stock returns are discontinuous
question: What happens to option prices if the stock can jump?
changed: Added Poisson jumps to the diffusion: the first model to produce a volatility smile, priced by assuming jump risk is diversifiable.

title: Options: A Monte Carlo approach
question: Can option prices be computed by simulation when no formula exists?
changed: Priced options as discounted averages of simulated risk-neutral payoffs, with variance reduction: the start of computational finance.

title: Prices of State-Contingent Claims Implicit in Option Prices
question: What do option prices across strikes say about the market's distribution?
changed: The second strike-derivative of the call price is the discounted risk-neutral density.

title: Option pricing: A simplified approach
question: Can option pricing be explained, and computed, without stochastic calculus?
changed: The binomial tree: replication one step at a time, converging to Black–Scholes and pricing American exercise by backward induction.

title: Option Pricing and Replication with Transactions Costs
question: What happens to continuous hedging when every trade costs money?
changed: Discrete hedging with proportional costs is priced by Black–Scholes with an adjusted volatility.

title: The Pricing of Options on Assets with Stochastic Volatilities
question: How do option prices change if volatility itself is random?
changed: With independent stochastic variance, the option price is Black–Scholes averaged over the distribution of realized variance.

title: A Closed-Form Solution for Options with Stochastic Volatility with Applications to Bond and Currency Options
question: Can a correlated stochastic-volatility model still be priced in closed form?
changed: Mean-reverting square-root variance correlated with the stock, priced through its characteristic function: skew from correlation.
assumed: Variance follows a CIR process; volatility risk has a linear price.

title: Pricing with a smile
question: Is there a diffusion that reproduces every quoted option price at once?
changed: Local volatility: a unique σ(S, t) recovered from the call surface by Dupire's formula.
assumed: Arbitrage-free prices for a continuum of strikes and expiries.

verified.note: Risk magazine article with no DOI; the link is Risk's own reprint.

title: Jumps and Stochastic Volatility: Exchange Rate Processes Implicit in Deutsche Mark Options
question: Does fitting real smiles need jumps as well as stochastic volatility?
changed: Combined Heston variance with Merton jumps; short-dated smiles need the jumps.

title: Option valuation using the fast Fourier transform
question: How do you price a whole strike grid quickly when only the characteristic function is known?
changed: Damp the call price, Fourier-transform it analytically, and use the FFT to get every strike at once.

title: Option Prices, Implied Price Processes, and Stochastic Volatility
question: Can expected future variance be read from options without a model?
changed: A strip of option prices across strikes gives risk-neutral expected integrated variance: the idea behind the VIX.

title: Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach
question: Can Monte Carlo handle early exercise?
changed: Estimate the continuation value by regressing discounted future cash flows on functions of the state, path by path.

title: Expected Option Returns
question: Do option returns match what the stock's risk alone implies?
changed: Index options, puts especially, lose far more than their beta predicts: volatility risk carries a price.

title: Managing Smile Risk
question: Why does local volatility hedge the smile badly, and what dynamics fix it?
changed: SABR: stochastic volatility with a backbone parameter and an asymptotic implied-vol formula, now the rates-market standard.

verified.note: Wilmott Magazine article with no DOI.

title: The Moment Formula for Implied Volatility at Extreme Strikes
question: How steep can the implied-variance smile be in the wings?
changed: Total implied variance grows at most linearly in log-strike, with slopes set by which moments of the price are finite.

title: A parsimonious arbitrage-free implied volatility parameterization with application to the valuation of volatility derivatives
question: Is there a five-parameter smile that fits equity markets and behaves in the wings?
changed: SVI: total implied variance as a hyperbola in log-moneyness, linear in the wings as Lee's formula requires.

title: Variance Risk Premiums
question: How much do investors pay to hedge variance?
changed: Synthetic variance swaps show realized variance sits well below implied: a large, negative variance risk premium.

title: Arbitrage-free SVI volatility surfaces
question: How do you fit a whole surface of SVI smiles without calendar or butterfly arbitrage?
changed: SSVI: a surface parameterization with explicit no-arbitrage conditions, and a recipe to repair raw SVI fits.

title: Volatility is rough
question: What does realized volatility look like at fine time scales?
changed: Log-volatility behaves like fractional Brownian motion with Hurst exponent near 0.1, far rougher than classical models.
